text:
alex: heads-up — saw p95 regressions on route:/chat/short after yesterday's kernel-prefetch tweak. p95 for small payloads jumped ~35% (98ms -> 132ms) on the free tier. not all routes affected.

mira: ugh. is this aligned with the new microbatcher switch? any kernel mismatch in profiler? :eyes:

raj: sharing a short perf dump — looks like more microbatches being formed (more batches of 1/2 tokens) and the kernel selector keeps picking the larger attention kernel, which increases prep overhead. KV hit rate also dropped ~6% around the same time.

raj: flame snippet: `prefetch_ms + kernel_swap_ms` spike correlates with queue hysteresis crossing. reproduced locally with synthetic short prompts (~10 tokens).

nicole: interesting — that suggests the dynamic token budget target is too aggressive for free-tier short routes. we should try reducing token_budget_multiplier for those routes and bump batch_hysteresis_ms so batches have time to coalesce.

alex: proposed canary config (YAML):
```
route_tiers:
  premium:
    token_budget_multiplier: "1.0"
    batch_hysteresis_ms: "8"
  free:
    token_budget_multiplier: "0.65"
    batch_hysteresis_ms: "22"
queue_policy:
  min_coalesce_tokens: "6"
  max_wait_ms: "40"
kernel_selector:
  prefer_small_seq_kernel_threshold: "32"
```

mira: two questions: 1) do we have SLO gating that will auto-fallback? 2) will this change KV warm-up behavior for prefix-heavy routes (e.g., embeddings-prepend)?

alex: 1) yes, the rollout will be behind slo-gateway canary with p95 check. 2) it might — increasing hysteresis lets more concurrent requests hit same GPU within prefix window, should improve KV hit rate for cacheable prefixes.

raj: ran quick microbench with the proposed free-tier knobs on a 10% canary image: p95 down to 105ms (from 132ms) for short-chat, KV hit recovered ~3%. throughput drop negligible. attaching perf numbers: `baseline:98/132/1.7k rps`, `canary:98/105/1.68k rps` (premium unchanged).

nicole: sounds promising. let's also tweak kernel_selector threshold to avoid choosing the heavy kernel for <32 seq. that should cut kernel_swap_ms.

alex: deploy-bot — start canary on fleet group `slo-prefetch-hysteresis-2026-03` at 10%
deploy-bot: Canary started on 10% of nodes (slo-prefetch-hysteresis-2026-03). monitoring p95 in /metrics/slo_chat_short. will report every 2m.

mira: pinging infra to make sure trace sampling is on for those instances so we can correlate recirculation events. @raj can you add a perf trace link when ready?

raj: will do — uploaded a perf flame + kv-hit histogram to the canary artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/slo-prefetch-hysteresis/1758881234

nicole: checklist for the rollout:
- [ ] run 2h canary at 10%
- [ ] validate p95 < 115ms on free short-chat route
- [ ] KV hit >= baseline - 2%
- [ ] no throughput regression on premium routes
- [ ] rollback plan ready (auto rollback if p95 worsens by >10%)

alex: if canary looks good after 2h we'll ramp to 40% and monitor 15m windows. if issues reappear, immediate rollback and we run narrower kernel-selector change.

mira: one more thought — add an instrumentation flag to emit `batch_formation_reason` (timer vs token_budget vs kernel_switch) for some fraction of requests. will help us debug cause vs symptom.

raj: added feature flag `emit_batch_reason=0.05` to canary config.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics: p95=107ms (2m avg), kv_hit=0.92 (2m avg), error_rate unchanged.

nicole: :thumbsup: good start. alex, please open a short postmortem if we need to roll forward the kernel-prefetch change with these new defaults. otherwise, we'll iterate on thresholds.

alex: will do. next steps: collect 2h canary, then ramp to 40% if stable. thanks all.

mira: noted ACTIONS: raj -> attach detailed perf artifacts + flame; alex -> PR for canary config; nicole -> prepare rollback runbook; infra -> ensure trace sampling.

raj: artifacts uploaded and linked in the canary channel.

nicole: filing rollback runbook now.

alex: closing loop here. thanks everyone. :)
